clue.text: Zero in maths worried Hardy, for one

indicators.note: the zero is placed in among the other letters
worried letters are fretted and churned, so the word maths is rearranged

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A student frets because they scored nothing in a maths exam, like the novelist did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges MATHS to THMAS, and 'in' puts O, the zero, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy was the Victorian novelist of Wessex, so Hardy is one person bearing that first name.

clue.text: Temperature, along with skin blemish, remains

parts.note: a rash is a skin eruption

explanation.surface: A fever with a rash is all that is left of an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Trash is rubbish, the waste or refuse left over.

clue.text: When clear outside, start to lift one blind

indicators.note: the clear word sits outside, around the other letters

parts.note: obvious means clear

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Raising a window blind when the sky outside is clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivious means unaware, blind to what is going on.

clue.text: Mythical vessel is back, crossing river

indicators.note: the past word stretches across the river letter, holding it

parts.note: ago means back in time, as in years back

explanation.surface: A legendary ship returns, crossing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a reversal sign but means AGO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth.

clue.text: Mistake to eat a cut of lamb that's salty

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the mistake word swallows the cut

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder
a rack of lamb is a cut of ribs

explanation.surface: A cook regrets a blunder: the lamb served is far too salty.
explanation.walkthrough: Bish is informal British slang for a blunder, little known outside the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Brackish water is slightly salt, as where river and sea water mix.

clue.text: One unable to fly into a passion turns to the bottle

indicators.note: the bird goes into the passion word

parts.note: rage is a passion of anger
the emu is a flightless bird

explanation.surface: A grounded person flies into a rage and takes to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns to the bottle' sounds like heavy drinking, but describes turning bottles in champagne making.
explanation.definitionFit: Remuage, or riddling, is the gradual twisting of champagne bottles to settle sediment in the neck.

clue.text: Run and hide in tell-tale city

parts.note: a canter is a horse's easy run
to bury something is to hide it

explanation.surface: A fugitive runs and hides in a city of gossips.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaucer's Canterbury Tales make it the city of tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Canterbury is the cathedral city of Chaucer's pilgrims' stories.

clue.text: Statue that is stuffed with paper item

indicators.note: the abbreviation is filled with the magazine word

parts.note: a mag, short for magazine, is a paper publication

explanation.surface: A statue is filled with papier-mache.
explanation.definitionFit: An image can be a carved figure or effigy, as in a graven image.

clue.text: Try and attend to nurse patient's last sign of life

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the pair of words cradle the letter

parts.note: a judge tries or hears a case
to be at is to attend

indicators.note: the patient's last is the final letter of the word patient

explanation.surface: A nurse tries to tend a patient whose last vital sign is fading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attend' is read as two words, be at; 'nurse' means hold, not care for.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartbeat is the pulse that shows a person is alive.

clue.text: Stone structure puzzling old people

indicators.note: puzzling describes something mixed up, so the letters of old are scrambled

parts.note: men means people

explanation.surface: An ancient monument baffles elderly visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolmen is a prehistoric tomb of upright stones capped by a flat slab.

clue.text: Brisk run expands one's whole self-image?

parts.note: whole means all

indicators.note: the run enlarges the self-image from inside, so it goes into it

parts.note: your ego is your sense of self
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A good run makes a person feel their whole sense of self is boosted.
explanation.walkthrough: The run goes into the self-image only, after the whole; 'one's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is a musical tempo marking meaning quick and lively.

clue.text: Physical structure shortly to be seen moving west across northern state

indicators.note: the reversed word stretches across the N, holding it inside
in an across clue, moving west means travelling right to left, so the letters are read backwards
cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: anatomy is the structure of a body

explanation.surface: A traveller's body is seen heading west through a northern US state.
explanation.walkthrough: ANATOMY shortened is ANATOM; 'moving west' turns it to MOTANA, which spans N.
explanation.definitionFit: Montana is a US state in the northern Rockies, on the Canadian border.

clue.text: Wretched dwelling, not large, in seaside resort

indicators.note: not large tells us to drop the letter for large

parts.note: a hovel is a squalid little house
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A miserable small house stands in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hove is a seaside town in Sussex, joined to Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Hove is an English coastal town on the south coast, a holiday destination.

clue.text: Spitting as article breaks piece of equipment

indicators.note: the article breaks into the tool word, sitting inside it

parts.note: an implement is a tool
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grammatical article interrupts a tool as it is used for skewering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spitting' is skewering on a spit, not saliva.
explanation.definitionFit: Impalement is piercing something through with a stake, as meat is run through on a roasting spit.

clue.text: Post Office insanely resited for remote islander

indicators.note: resited means moved to another place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A post office is moved, absurdly, for someone on a distant island.
explanation.definitionFit: Polynesians are natives of the far-flung Pacific island groups.

clue.text: Declare liable for docking cat

indicators.note: for here means taking in, the liable word holding the cat

parts.note: prone means liable or inclined

indicators.note: docking a tail cuts it off, so the final letter goes

parts.note: an ounce is the snow leopard

explanation.surface: Someone states they are liable for cutting a cat's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The ounce is the snow leopard, a crossword favourite cat; docking it means losing its tail letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to announce formally, as a judge pronounces sentence.

clue.text: Assistant forbidding bringing dog over for hair styling

indicators.note: bringing the dog moves it in front of the assistant
over places the dog before the assistant in the down entry

parts.note: pom is short for Pomeranian, a toy dog
PA is a personal assistant
dour means grim, forbidding

explanation.surface: A stern assistant brings a dog to be groomed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a hairstyle swept up high from the forehead.

clue.text: What's needed for job — a steel tack

indicators.note: the answer is something contained in the following words, which carry its letters within them

explanation.surface: A workman lists what the job requires: a steel tack.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'job a steel', ignoring the dash.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste is to sew with long loose stitches, the same as tacking fabric in place.

clue.text: Keeping calm if dragons run wild

indicators.note: letters that run wild are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Stay composed even if dragons go on the rampage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangfroid is composure under stress, literally cold blood.

clue.text: A year after "essential," stale

indicators.note: the year comes after the essential word

parts.note: a must is an essential thing
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Something essential goes stale once a year has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Musty describes a damp, mouldy smell, like stale air in a shut room.

clue.text: Moving eyes, trademark completion of portrait: his?

definitions.text: Moving eyes, trademark completion of portrait: his?

parts.note: REM is rapid eye movement
a brand is a trademark

indicators.note: the completion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Eyes that follow you and a signature finish: whose portrait is it?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the painter's portraits, with their lifelike eyes and signature touches.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt was the Dutch master famous for portraits and self-portraits.

clue.text: Chatters away but sounds insecure

definitions.meaning: second meaning: makes a clattering noise as something loose does

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is talking incessantly; the other is the clatter of a loose part.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both nonstop prattle and the knocking noise of something not firmly fixed.

clue.text: Nightmare as revolutionary spirit rises

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read bottom to top

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A bad dream as a revolutionary mood grows.
explanation.walkthrough: REDRUM read upwards; a nod to The Shining.
explanation.definitionFit: Murder is used informally of something awful, a real ordeal.

clue.text: Sickness moving one indeed to eat right, being concerned with nutrition

indicators.note: the I is shifted to a new place in the sickness word

parts.note: an ailment is an illness
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the indeed word takes the right letter inside

parts.note: ay means yes, indeed

explanation.surface: An illness indeed makes one eat properly, a dietary matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving one' shifts the I in AILMENT to give ALIMENT; then AY eats R to give ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimentary relates to food and digestion, as in the alimentary canal.

clue.text: In this group of languages charge is incomplete

indicators.note: incomplete means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to indict is to charge formally

explanation.surface: Within this language family, a charge is left unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Indic is the branch of Indo-European including Hindi and Sanskrit.

clue.text: Some animals fancied each way at the start

indicators.note: only the first letter of each of the four words is used

explanation.surface: A racing tip: back the fancied animals each way.
explanation.walkthrough: Each way is a racing bet on a win or a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A few means a small number, just as some can mean several.

clue.text: Savage conserves energy to use as a weapon

indicators.note: conserves means keeps safe within, holding the energy letter

parts.note: wild means savage
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A savage saves his energy to use as a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To wield is to handle and brandish a sword or tool.

clue.text: Old friend is a gem

parts.note: pal means friend

explanation.surface: An old friend is a treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is an iridescent precious stone.

clue.text: Proposed law from long ago in force

parts.note: old means of long ago
a bill is a law proposed in parliament

explanation.surface: An old parliamentary bill is still in force.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bill is British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The police force is known colloquially in Britain by this nickname.

clue.text: Lose it completely, chucking policeman in river

indicators.note: chucking means throwing, and the officer is thrown into the river
the policeman ends up inside the river word

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
plod is British slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: An enraged person throws a policeman into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, England; PLOD is slang for a constable.
explanation.definitionFit: To explode is to burst out in rage, completely losing your temper.

clue.text: Regularly ruin board game, introducing new complexity

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the following word
the game brings the new letter in among its own

parts.note: chess is played on a board

explanation.surface: A spoilt game of chess becomes more involved with a new move.
explanation.definitionFit: Richness of texture or flavour is its depth and intricacy.

clue.text: Youngster in cot, perhaps with sharp edge

indicators.note: the boy sits inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is one kind of bed
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A child lies in a cot, perhaps holding something sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Bladed means having a blade, a cutting edge like a knife.
